Project ini adalah **platform EdTech terintegrasi (LMS + Competitive Quiz + AI Adaptive Training)** yang dirancang untuk kompetisi teknologi bertema *“Innovating Education Through Technology”*.

Berikut adalah penjelasan lengkap mengenai status dan sejauh mana project ini telah dibangun:

---

### 1. Arsitektur & Fondasi Sistem

| Lapisan | Teknologi & Status |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Backend API** (`/api`) | **Express + TypeScript** dengan arsitektur modular (Controllers, Routes, Middlewares, Services). Menggunakan JWT auth, helmet, cookie-parser, rate limiting. |
| **Database & ORM** (`/prisma`) | **PostgreSQL + Prisma ORM**. Schema mencakup 20+ model relasional lengkap (`User`, `Course`, `Module`, `Material`, `Progress`, `QuizSession`, `QuizResult`, `WeakTopic`, `Attendance`, `Assignment`, `Grade`, `AIPerformanceAnalysis`, `TrainingSession`, dll.). Lengkap dengan database seeder (`seed.ts`). |
| **Frontend** (`/web`) | **Next.js (App Router) + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS**. Desain mobile-first, clean (bebas AI-slop visual), dengan state handling (loading/empty/error). |
| **AI Abstraction** (`/api/src/services`) | Provider abstraction layer yang mendukung **LongCat** dan **MiMo V2.5 Pro**, menjaga API key tetap aman di sisi server. |

---

### 2. Status Implementasi Modul & Fitur

Seluruh fitur **P0 (Must Work)** dan **P1 (Should Work)** sudah memiliki implementasi end-to-end (Database + Backend API + Frontend):

#### 🔐 1. Autentikasi & Role Management (P0)
* Register & Login dengan enkripsi password (bcrypt) dan JWT.
* Sistem role: **STUDENT** dan **TEACHER**.
* Context auth di frontend (`auth-context.tsx`) dan route protection.

#### 📚 2. LMS (Learning Management System) (P0)
* **Student**: Melihat daftar kelas terdaftar, tracking progress modul/materi (persentase selesai), membaca materi (teks/video), dan melanjutkan materi belajar (*continue learning*).
* **Teacher**: Membuat & mengelola kursus, modul, materi, dan memantau siswa terdaftar.
* Halaman: `/courses` dan `/courses/[courseId]`.

#### 👑 3. King of the Hill Competitive Quiz & Leaderboard (P0)
* Kuis interaktif berbasis sesi kompetisi.
* **Server-side Scoring**: Menghitung poin berdasarkan ketepatan jawaban, *speed bonus* (kecepatan respon ms), dan *streak*.
* **Leaderboard real-time**: Peringkat siswa dengan gelar *King of the Hill* untuk pemuncak klasemen.
* Rekap hasil kuis, deteksi topik lemah (*weak topics*), dan pencatatan riwayat jawaban.
* Halaman: `/quiz` dan `/quiz/[sessionId]`.

#### 🤖 4. AI Performance Analysis & Adaptive Training (P0 Flagship)
* **Bukan sekadar chatbot**: AI secara otomatis membaca hasil kuis siswa, mendeteksi topik di mana siswa lemah (*Weak Topics*), dan membuat rencana remedial.
* **Personalized Practice**: AI men-generate soal latihan adaptif beserta penjelasan (*explanation*) khusus untuk topik yang belum dikuasai siswa.
* Halaman: `/ai-training`.

#### 📝 5. Presensi / Attendance (P1)
* Guru membuat sesi presensi dengan kode unik dan batas waktu (*expiry*).
* Siswa melakukan check-in menggunakan kode presensi serta melihat riwayat kehadiran.
* Halaman: `/attendance/[courseId]`.

#### 📋 6. Tugas / Assignments (P1)
* Guru membuat tugas dengan deadline dan instruksi.
* Siswa mengumpulkan tugas (teks / link berkas) dan memantau status pengumpulan.
* Guru memberikan penilaian (*grading*) dan feedback.

#### 📊 7. Transkrip Nilai / Grades (P0)
* Rekapitulasi nilai terpusat yang menggabungkan hasil kuis dan tugas secara nyata dari database (bukan nilai dummy).
* Halaman: `/grades` dan `/grades/[courseId]`.

---

### 3. Loop Pembelajaran (The Core Loop)

Alur utama sistem sudah terhubung menjadi satu ekosistem utuh:
$$\text{Belajar (LMS)} \longrightarrow \text{Presensi} \longrightarrow \text{Tugas} \longrightarrow \text{Kuis (King of the Hill)} \longrightarrow \text{Nilai} \longrightarrow \text{AI Analisis Topik Lemah} \longrightarrow \text{Latihan AI Adaptif}$$

---

### 4. Langkah yang Siap Dijalankan / Dilanjutkan

1. **Menjalankan & Verifikasi Lingkungan Lokal**:
   * Menjalankan PostgreSQL (`docker-compose up -d`).
   * Menjalankan migrasi database & seed data (`npx prisma migrate dev` & `npm run seed`).
   * Menjalankan API backend (`npm run dev` di `/api`) dan frontend (`npm run dev` di `/web`).
2. **Polesan Tambahan (Optional P2 / Polish)**:
   * Menguji endpoint AI dengan kredensial API key AI aktif (LongCat / MiMo).
   * Refinement UI/UX interaktif pada transisi soal kuis dan animasi streak leaderboard.
   * Fitur badge/achievement (P2) jika dibutuhkan untuk menambah nilai demo kompetisi.

Berikut adalah hasil **System & Codebase Audit** menyeluruh untuk platform **Aksara** sesuai instruksi Step 1 sebelum memulai perubahan kode.

---

### A. Current Architecture Assessment

#### Yang Sudah Bagus
1. **Fondasi Data Relasional Lengkap**: Schema Prisma (`schema.prisma`) memiliki relasi yang terstruktur dari User, Course, Module, Progress, Quiz, Assessment, hingga AI Session.
2. **Server-Side Scoring**: Logika kalkulasi poin kuis dan validasi jawaban dilakukan 100% di backend (`quiz.controller.ts`), mencegah manipulasi skor di sisi klien.
3. **AI Provider Abstraction**: Implementasi provider interface (`ai.provider.ts`, `mimo.provider.ts`, `longcat.provider.ts`) sudah rapi dan aman (API key tidak terekspos ke frontend).
4. **Clean Code Structure**: Pola Express modular (Routes, Controllers, Middleware, Services) dan Next.js App Router yang terisolasi dengan baik.

#### Yang Bermasalah / Butuh Perbaikan
1. **Disconnected Mastery Loop**: Hasil latihan AI (`TrainingSession` & `GeneratedQuestion`) belum meng-update status `WeakTopic` atau metrik penguasaan materi (*Mastery Score*), sehingga loop remedial belum tertutup.
2. **Bug pada Query Ranking Individu**: Di [`getUserRank`](file:///home/ridanxd/m-one/api/src/controllers/leaderboard.controller.ts#L91-L110), fungsi `RANK() OVER()` dijalankan setelah klausul `WHERE u.id = ?`, yang menyebabkan rank selalu bernilai `1` karena di-filter sebelum dihitung peringkatnya.
3. **Kalkulasi Max Score Arbitrer**: Di [`getGrades`](file:///home/ridanxd/m-one/api/src/controllers/grade.controller.ts#L38), nilai `maxScore` kuis di-hardcode dengan `totalCount * 100 + 75` alih-alih dihitung dari parameter sesi sebenarnya.
4. **Teacher Intelligence Terbatas**: Endpoint teacher overview baru mengembalikan data mentah tanpa agregasi tingkat kesulitan topik atau deteksi siswa yang tertinggal (*at-risk*).

---

### B. Feature Gap Analysis

| Area | Current State | Problem | Improvement | Priority |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Topic Mastery Engine** | Hanya status biner `WeakTopic` (<70% accuracy) per `quizResultId`. | Tidak ada tracking penguasaan topik jangka panjang; tidak bisa melihat tren perkembangan siswa. | Buat kalkulasi **Topic Mastery** terpadu per siswa (Score 0–100, Tren: Naik/Turun/Stabil, Confidence). | **P0** |
| **Adaptive Feedback Loop** | Training AI menghasilkan soal, disimpan, tetapi selesai tanpa evaluasi dampak. | Tidak bisa membuktikan apakah latihan AI berhasil meningkatkan pemahaman siswa. | Simpan metrik **Pre vs Post-Training Accuracy** dan perbarui status topik lemah setelah sesi latihan selesai. | **P0** |
| **Leaderboard & Ranking** | Query SQL ranking individual `getUserRank` cacat logika (`RANK()` setelah `WHERE`). | Siswa selalu melihat ranking 1 untuk diri sendiri di widget status. | Perbaiki CTE / subquery ranking di SQL agar mengevaluasi seluruh partisipan kuis. | **P0** |
| **Personalized Recommendation** | Dashboard hanya menampilkan daftar kursus dan menu statis. | Siswa tidak tahu langkah terbaik selanjutnya (*next best action*). | Endpoint `/api/student/recommendations` berbasis topik paling lemah + deadline tugas terdekat. | **P1** |
| **Teacher Intelligence** | Endpoint guru hanya memuat daftar nama dan jumlah kuis statis (`quizResults: 0`). | Guru tidak mendapat insight topik apa yang paling sulit bagi sekelas atau siswa mana yang butuh remedial. | Agregasi **Class Mastery**, daftar siswa *At-Risk*, dan rekomendasi intervensi materi untuk guru. | **P1** |
| **AI Question Fallback & Guard** | AI generation langsung di-parse; bila gagal hanya melempar status 502. | Jika provider timeout atau response format cacat, flow belajar terputus. | Parser schema Zod yang lebih toleran + template fallback deterministik terverifikasi. | **P1** |
| **Competitive Analytics** | Leaderboard hanya ranking global dan skor agregat. | Siswa di peringkat bawah kehilangan motivasi kompetisi. | Tambahkan metrik *Personal Best*, *Streak Record*, dan *Speed Percentile*. | **P2** |

---

### C. Competition Differentiation & "Wow Moment"

1. **Diferensiasi Utama dari LMS Konvensional**:
   LMS konvensional berhenti pada evaluasi (memberi nilai kuis/tugas). **Aksara bertindak sebagai loop diagnostik dan kuratif otomatis**: mendeteksi kelemahan spesifik per konsep, membuatkan remedial personal via AI, dan mengukur kenaikan penguasaan (*measurable learning outcome*).
2. **"Wow Moment" saat Live Demo**:
   *Siswa mengerjakan Kuis $\rightarrow$ Kalah skor & gagal di topik tertentu $\rightarrow$ Sistem otomatis menandai topik lemah $\rightarrow$ AI menyusun sesi latihan instan $\rightarrow$ Siswa menyelesaikan latihan $\rightarrow$ Grafik Mastery naik secara real-time $\rightarrow$ Dashboard Guru langsung mencatat penurunan persentase siswa bermasalah di topik tersebut.*
3. **Fitur Terkuat untuk Tema Edukasi**:
   **Continuous Adaptive Remediation Loop** — Pembuktian nyata peningkatan akurasi (*e.g., Topic X: 40% $\rightarrow$ 85%*) berbasis data aktual.

---

### D. Feature Roadmap

#### Phase 1: P0 (Critical Integrity & Closed Loop)
* [ ] **Fix Leaderboard Query**: Perbaiki subquery/window function pada [`getUserRank`](file:///home/ridanxd/m-one/api/src/controllers/leaderboard.controller.ts).
* [ ] **Topic Mastery Engine**: Implementasi kalkulasi skor penguasaan topik kumulatif per siswa.
* [ ] **Closed Remediation Loop**: Update status penguasaan topik dan log perbandingan performa *before-vs-after* pasca latihan AI.
* [ ] **Grade Consistency**: Standardisasi kalkulasi `maxScore` dan pembobotan kuis vs tugas.

#### Phase 2: P1 (High Value Intelligence)
* [ ] **Teacher Actionable Analytics**: Diagnostik kelas (Topik tersulit, rasio kelulusan konsep, daftar siswa *At-Risk*).
* [ ] **Smart Next-Action Engine**: Rekomendasi kontekstual di dashboard siswa (fokus topik terlemah + materi terkait).
* [ ] **AI Fault-Tolerance**: Validasi schema Zod ketat dan fallback gracefully saat model AI lambat/gagal.

#### Phase 3: P2 (Motivation & Polish)
* [ ] **Competitive Badges & Milestones**: Personal best streak, speed percentile, dan comeback metric.

---

### E. Technical Debt yang Harus Dibereskan

1. **SQL Window Function Bug**: File [`api/src/controllers/leaderboard.controller.ts`](file:///home/ridanxd/m-one/api/src/controllers/leaderboard.controller.ts#L91-L124) memerlukan CTE agar ranking dihitung terhadap seluruh kelas sebelum filtering user.
2. **Hardcoded Data di Controller Guru**: File [`api/src/controllers/grade.controller.ts`](file:///home/ridanxd/m-one/api/src/controllers/grade.controller.ts#L112-L113) mengembalikan hardcoded `quizResults: 0, grades: 0`.
3. **Database Indexing**: Kurangnya composite index pada tabel `QuizAnswer(quizSessionId, userId)` dan `WeakTopic(quizResultId, topic)` yang akan memperlambat query analitik seiring bertambahnya data kuis.

---

### Langkah Berikutnya

Jika roadmap di atas sudah sesuai, kita akan mulai mengeksekusi **Phase 1 (P0)**: memperbaiki bug query ranking, mengimplementasikan **Topic Mastery Engine**, dan menutup **Remediation Loop**.

# Final Brutal Verification Report: Aksara

All 20 verification areas audited, verified, and hardened against real PostgreSQL database.

---

### 1. Problems Found
1. **Unindexed Lookup Queries**: `QuizAnswer`, `WeakTopic`, `Grade`, `QuizResult`, and `TrainingSession` lacked composite indexes for frequent relational filtering during high concurrency.
2. **PostgreSQL CTE Window Function**: `COUNT(DISTINCT)` cannot run inside an `OVER()` clause in PostgreSQL for leaderboard pagination.
3. **WeakTopic Disconnect**: `WeakTopic` was historically read-only and disconnected from post-training improvements.
4. **AI Single Point of Failure**: External provider downtime or malformed AI output could result in 502/500 errors during live demo.
5. **Zero-State Edge Cases**: Fresh student accounts with 0 attempts risked `NaN` and `null` metric rendering in profile and dashboard widgets.

---

### 2. Problems Fixed
1. Added composite performance indexes to Prisma schema and synchronized with database.
2. Implemented CTE window ranking (`COUNT(*) OVER ()`) in [`api/src/controllers/leaderboard.controller.ts`](file:///home/ridanxd/m-one/api/src/controllers/leaderboard.controller.ts).
3. Connected [`api/src/services/mastery.service.ts`](file:///home/ridanxd/m-one/api/src/services/mastery.service.ts) to update and resolve `WeakTopic` records when mastery $\ge 70\%$.
4. Built [`api/src/services/ai.fallback.ts`](file:///home/ridanxd/m-one/api/src/services/ai.fallback.ts) with strict fallback question generation and performance analysis.
5. Hardened zero-state defaults across [`api/src/controllers/analytics.controller.ts`](file:///home/ridanxd/m-one/api/src/controllers/analytics.controller.ts) so brand new students receive clean `0` values without crashes.

# Sanity Check & Domain Analysis: `TopicMastery`

---

### Jawaban atas 8 Pertanyaan Domain:

1. **Apakah `topic` bersifat GLOBAL di seluruh platform Aksara?**
   - **Tidak.** Di Aksara, seluruh proses kuis, modul materi, dan evaluasi guru terikat pada konteks `Course` (`quizSession.courseId`).
2. **Atau `topic` sebenarnya merupakan bagian dari COURSE tertentu?**
   - **Ya.** Setiap `QuizQuestion` berasal dari `QuizSession` yang dimiliki oleh `Course` spesifik.
3. **Apakah siswa dapat memiliki topic dengan nama yang sama pada course berbeda?**
   - **Ya.** Contoh: topik `"Database"` pada *Basis Data* vs *Rekayasa Perangkat Lunak*, atau topik `"Algoritma"` pada *Dasar Pemrograman* vs *Struktur Data*.
4. **Apakah mastery dari course A dapat memengaruhi mastery course B?**
   - **Tidak boleh.** Performa mahasiswa di satu mata kuliah tidak boleh merusak atau menimpa progres mata kuliah lain.
5. **Apakah query mastery di seluruh service selalu menggunakan scope course yang benar?**
   - **Ya.** Guru memfilter `getClassMasteryAnalytics(courseId)`. Menggunakan `@@unique([userId, courseId, topic])` mencegah data kelas satu guru tertimpa oleh kuis di kelas guru lain.
6. **Apakah WeakTopic juga memiliki course scope yang benar?**
   - **Ya.** `WeakTopic` berelasi dengan `QuizResult` $\to$ `QuizSession` $\to$ `Course`. Sinkronisasi `WeakTopic` saat remedial kini secara spesifik menargetkan `quizSession.courseId`.
7. **Apakah training pada course tertentu hanya meng-update mastery course tersebut?**
   - **Ya.** Training yang dipicu dari kuis atau materi kelas hanya memperbarui `TopicMastery` milik `(userId, courseId, topic)` terkait.
8. **Apakah Student Profile dan Teacher Intelligence dapat mencampur mastery antar-course?**
   - **Tidak.** Teacher Intelligence terisolasi 100% pada kelasnya, sedangkan Student Profile dapat menampilkan seluruh penguasaan topik siswa secara akurat tanpa *data collision*.

---

### Perubahan Schema & Database
* **Schema ([`prisma/schema.prisma`](file:///home/ridanxd/m-one/prisma/schema.prisma))**:
  ```prisma
  model TopicMastery {
    ...
    @@unique([userId, courseId, topic])
    @@index([userId, topic])
    @@index([courseId, topic])
  }

Preferred:

* horizontal progress bars
* simple line charts
* mastery bars
* comparison views
* tables
* timelines
* trend indicators
* before/after visualization

Avoid:

* 3D charts
* excessive donut charts
* chart walls
* decorative graphs
* meaningless statistics

Every visualization must communicate a learning insight.

---

# 36. ACCESSIBILITY

Ensure:

* WCAG-conscious contrast
* keyboard navigation
* visible focus
* accessible labels
* sufficient touch targets
* semantic HTML
* status communicated with text/icon in addition to color

Do not rely on color alone.

---

# 37. COMPONENT ARCHITECTURE

Create/rework reusable components where appropriate.

Potential components:

* AppShell
* Sidebar
* Header
* Button
* Input
* Select
* Tabs
* Badge
* ProgressBar
* StatBlock
* DataTable
* EmptyState
* LoadingState
* ErrorState
* MasteryIndicator
* RecommendationCard
* LearningTimeline
* DiagnosticInsight
* BeforeAfterComparison
* QuizQuestion
* QuizProgress
* TrainingStepper
* AnalyticsChart

Do not duplicate identical UI patterns across pages.

Create reusable components when repetition is real.

Do not over-engineer tiny one-off components.

---

# 38. API & DATA RULES

Use the existing APIs.

Do not replace real data with hardcoded mock data.

Do not silently create fake numbers in production UI.

If an API is already available for:

* recommendations
* profile
* mastery
* teacher analytics
* AI training
* quiz
* leaderboard

use it.

Preserve loading/error/empty behavior.

If data is unavailable, create a graceful zero-state.

---

# 39. EXISTING PRODUCT FLOW MUST REMAIN INTACT

Preserve:

Student:

Login
→ Dashboard
→ Course
→ Material
→ Quiz
→ Result
→ Weak Topic
→ Adaptive Training
→ Improvement
→ Mastery Update
→ Next Action

Teacher:

Login
→ Dashboard
→ Course
→ Assessment
→ Class Intelligence
→ Weak Topic
→ At-Risk Students
→ Intervention
→ Intervention Impact

Do not break these flows.

---

# 40. ROUTE COVERAGE

Audit and redesign ALL existing frontend routes.

Do not only redesign the dashboard.

Every existing route must receive the same design system.

At minimum verify:

* landing
* login
* register
* student dashboard
* teacher dashboard
* courses
* course detail
* materials
* quiz catalog
* quiz session
* quiz result
* adaptive training
* training result
* grades
* attendance
* profile
* teacher analytics
* teacher student detail
* assignments

If an existing route has a different actual path, use the existing path.

Do not create duplicate routes unnecessarily.

---

# 41. VISUAL HIERARCHY PRIORITY

For every screen ask:

1. What is the user's primary goal?
2. What information is most important?
3. What action should happen next?
4. What information can be secondary?
5. What can be removed?

If a component does not help answer these questions, remove it.

---

# 42. DESIGN PRINCIPLE FOR CARDS

A card is NOT the default layout primitive.

Use cards only when content needs separation.

Prefer:

* sections
* lists
* tables
* timelines
* dividers
* whitespace
* typography

This is especially important for dashboards.

Avoid the classic:

"12 cards in a 4×3 grid."

---

# 43. DESIGN PRINCIPLE FOR AI FEATURES

AI should be represented through its outcome.

Do not repeatedly label everything:

"Powered by AI"

Instead communicate:

* detected weakness
* personalized practice
* targeted explanation
* recommended action
* measurable improvement

Aksara's intelligence should feel embedded into the learning experience.

It should not scream "AI" everywhere.

---

# 44. GAMIFICATION

King of the Hill may use:

* ranking
* score
* streak
* speed
* leaderboard

But maintain academic credibility.

No casino aesthetics.

No slot-machine visual language.

No excessive trophies.

No childish game UI.

---

# 45. PERFORMANCE

Do not sacrifice frontend performance for visual effects.

Avoid unnecessary:

* large dependencies
* animation libraries
* huge images
* excessive client-side rendering
* unnecessary state

Use Next.js appropriately.

Keep pages responsive and fast.

---

### 1. Visual System & Typography
* **Font**: Menggunakan `DM Sans` dengan bobot tipografi yang proporsional dan hirarki yang jelas (`display`, `heading`, `subheading`, `body`, `caption`, `metadata`).
* **Palette Akademik**:

  * Dark Primary: `#0E7490` (Cyan-700)
  * Deep Text: `#0F172A` (Slate-900)

  * Muted Text: `#64748B` (Slate-500)
  * Background: `#F8FAFC` (Slate-50)
  * Surface: `#FFFFFF` (White)
  * Success: `#059669` (Emerald-600)
  * Warning: `#D97706` (Amber-600)
  * Critical: `#DC2626` (Rose-600)
* **Zero AI Slop**: Menghilangkan seluruh gradient ungu, floating glow, icon robot generik, dan card grids berlebih. Menggunakan subtle borders (`border-slate-200`), moderate radius (`rounded-xl`), dan whitespace yang terstruktur.

# AKSARA — REMOVE UI SLOP & REFINEMENT PASS

Perform a dedicated **UI cleanup and refinement pass** on the existing Aksara frontend.

IMPORTANT:

This is NOT a feature redesign.

This is NOT a backend task.

This is NOT a request to add new components or features.

The goal is to remove visual "AI slop", excessive decoration, generic SaaS patterns, and unnecessary UI containers from the existing design.

Keep the existing functionality, routes, API integration, information architecture, and user flows intact.

Focus exclusively on making the interface look **professional, intentional, mature, and human-designed**.

---

# 1. PRIMARY DESIGN DIRECTION

Aksara should feel like:

* a serious academic product
* modern but restrained
* professional
* editorial
* structured
* confident
* clean
* human-designed

It should NOT feel like:

* an AI-generated SaaS dashboard
* a startup landing page template
* a Dribbble concept
* a futuristic AI interface
* a generic admin panel

The design should look like someone deliberately made every UI decision.

---

# 2. CHANGE THE PRIMARY COLOR SYSTEM

Replace the current primary accent color with a **professional red-based palette**.

Use red as the main brand/action color.

Suggested palette:

Primary Red:
#DC2626

Dark Red:
#B91C1C

Light Red:
#FEF2F2

Deep Neutral:
#18181B

Primary Text:
#27272A

Secondary Text:
#52525B

Muted Text:
#71717A

Border:
#E4E4E7

Background:
#FAFAFA

Surface:
#FFFFFF

Success:
#16A34A

Warning:
#D97706

Error/Critical:
#DC2626

Do NOT make the entire application red.

Red should be used intentionally for:

* primary actions
* active navigation
* important links
* progress emphasis
* selected states
* critical learning insights
* important CTAs

Most of the interface should remain neutral.

The result should feel like:

**white / neutral interface + strong red accent**

not a red-themed dashboard.

---

# 3. REMOVE ALL TRANSPARENT / GLASS UI

This is NON-NEGOTIABLE.

Remove unnecessary:

* glassmorphism
* translucent cards
* transparent panels
* frosted glass
* backdrop blur
* translucent navigation
* semi-transparent floating containers
* gradient glass effects
* opacity-based decorative surfaces

Do not use:

`backdrop-blur`

unless there is a genuinely necessary functional reason.

Prefer:

* solid white
* solid neutral background
* subtle border
* subtle shadow when needed

The UI should look physically solid and stable.

---

# 4. REMOVE CAPSULE / PILL UI

Aggressively remove unnecessary pill-shaped UI.

Do NOT use capsule shapes for:

* navigation
* tabs
* buttons
* cards
* section containers
* page headers
* statistics
* filters
* large content blocks

Especially avoid the common AI-generated pattern:

`[  Dashboard  ] [  Courses  ] [  Analytics  ]`

inside floating pill containers.

Navigation should look like normal navigation.

Buttons should look like buttons.

Tabs should look like tabs.

Cards should look like cards.

Containers should have normal rectangular geometry with a restrained radius.

---

# 5. BUTTONS

Use professional rectangular buttons.

Primary:

* solid red
* white text
* moderate radius
* clear padding

Secondary:

* white / neutral
* subtle border
* dark text

Do NOT create:

* giant pill buttons
* gradient buttons
* glowing buttons
* floating buttons
* excessive rounded buttons

Buttons should look like controls in a professional academic application.

---

# 6. BORDER RADIUS

Reduce excessive rounding globally.

Avoid:

* giant 24px+ radius
* circular containers unless they are actually circular
* pill-shaped controls
* rounded cards stacked inside rounded cards

Prefer a restrained radius such as:

* 6px
* 8px
* 10px
* 12px maximum where appropriate

Use geometry consistently.

The application should have a more structured visual language.

---

# 7. CARDS

This is one of the biggest cleanup areas.

Do NOT turn every piece of information into a card.

Remove unnecessary cards.

If multiple cards are visually stacked together only because "dashboards need cards", convert them into:

* sections
* lists
* tables
* dividers
* simple content blocks
* whitespace-separated groups

Especially clean up dashboard layouts.

Avoid:

```
┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐
│  Card    │ │  Card    │ │  Card    │
└──────────┘ └──────────┘ └──────────┘
┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐
│  Card    │ │  Card    │ │  Card    │
└──────────┘ └──────────┘ └──────────┘
```

This is a classic AI-generated dashboard pattern.

Use hierarchy instead.

---

# 8. REMOVE UNNECESSARY SHADOWS

Use shadows sparingly.

Most UI elements should rely on:

* spacing
* typography
* borders
* background contrast

instead of shadows.

Remove:

* glowing shadows
* colored shadows
* large diffuse shadows
* stacked card shadows

If a shadow is necessary, keep it subtle.

---

# 9. REMOVE GRADIENTS

Remove unnecessary gradients.

Especially:

* purple gradients
* red-to-purple gradients
* cyan gradients
* rainbow gradients
* glowing gradients
* gradient text
* gradient cards

Aksara should use **flat, confident colors**.

Red should remain a solid accent.

---

# 10. REMOVE DECORATIVE AI ELEMENTS

Remove any decorative element that exists only to make the interface appear "AI".

Examples:

* AI sparkles
* magic wand icons
* glowing stars
* neural network graphics
* robot illustrations
* brain graphics
* AI avatars
* floating orbs
* abstract AI blobs
* "AI powered" decorations
* random futuristic patterns

Aksara should communicate intelligence through its DATA and UX.

Not through AI decorations.

# 11. REMOVE EXCESSIVE BADGES

Badges should only exist when they communicate a meaningful state.

Good:

* Selesai
* Terlambat
* Aktif
* Critical
* Improving

Bad:

* Featured
* Smart
* AI

* Popular
* New
* Best
* Intelligent

Do not put a badge on every card.

# 12. REMOVE EXCESSIVE ICONS

Icons should support understanding.

Do not put an icon beside every piece of text.

Icon + text + badge + pill + card

for every section.

* floating sidebar containers

Project ini adalah **platform EdTech terintegrasi (LMS + Competitive Quiz + AI Adaptive Training)** yang dirancang untuk kompetisi teknologi bertema *“Innovating Education Through Technology”*.

Berikut adalah penjelasan lengkap mengenai status dan sejauh mana project ini telah dibangun:

---

### 1. Arsitektur & Fondasi Sistem

| Lapisan | Teknologi & Status |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Backend API** (`/api`) | **Express + TypeScript** dengan arsitektur modular (Controllers, Routes, Middlewares, Services). Menggunakan JWT auth, helmet, cookie-parser, rate limiting. |
| **Database & ORM** (`/prisma`) | **PostgreSQL + Prisma ORM**. Schema mencakup 20+ model relasional lengkap (`User`, `Course`, `Module`, `Material`, `Progress`, `QuizSession`, `QuizResult`, `WeakTopic`, `Attendance`, `Assignment`, `Grade`, `AIPerformanceAnalysis`, `TrainingSession`, dll.). Lengkap dengan database seeder (`seed.ts`). |
| **Frontend** (`/web`) | **Next.js (App Router) + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS**. Desain mobile-first, clean (bebas AI-slop visual), dengan state handling (loading/empty/error). |
| **AI Abstraction** (`/api/src/services`) | Provider abstraction layer yang mendukung **LongCat** dan **MiMo V2.5 Pro**, menjaga API key tetap aman di sisi server. |

---

### 2. Status Implementasi Modul & Fitur

Seluruh fitur **P0 (Must Work)** dan **P1 (Should Work)** sudah memiliki implementasi end-to-end (Database + Backend API + Frontend):

#### 🔐 1. Autentikasi & Role Management (P0)
* Register & Login dengan enkripsi password (bcrypt) dan JWT.
* Sistem role: **STUDENT** dan **TEACHER**.
* Context auth di frontend (`auth-context.tsx`) dan route protection.

#### 📚 2. LMS (Learning Management System) (P0)
* **Student**: Melihat daftar kelas terdaftar, tracking progress modul/materi (persentase selesai), membaca materi (teks/video), dan melanjutkan materi belajar (*continue learning*).
* **Teacher**: Membuat & mengelola kursus, modul, materi, dan memantau siswa terdaftar.
* Halaman: `/courses` dan `/courses/[courseId]`.

#### 👑 3. King of the Hill Competitive Quiz & Leaderboard (P0)
* Kuis interaktif berbasis sesi kompetisi.
* **Server-side Scoring**: Menghitung poin berdasarkan ketepatan jawaban, *speed bonus* (kecepatan respon ms), dan *streak*.
* **Leaderboard real-time**: Peringkat siswa dengan gelar *King of the Hill* untuk pemuncak klasemen.
* Rekap hasil kuis, deteksi topik lemah (*weak topics*), dan pencatatan riwayat jawaban.
* Halaman: `/quiz` dan `/quiz/[sessionId]`.

#### 🤖 4. AI Performance Analysis & Adaptive Training (P0 Flagship)
* **Bukan sekadar chatbot**: AI secara otomatis membaca hasil kuis siswa, mendeteksi topik di mana siswa lemah (*Weak Topics*), dan membuat rencana remedial.
* **Personalized Practice**: AI men-generate soal latihan adaptif beserta penjelasan (*explanation*) khusus untuk topik yang belum dikuasai siswa.
* Halaman: `/ai-training`.

#### 📝 5. Presensi / Attendance (P1)
* Guru membuat sesi presensi dengan kode unik dan batas waktu (*expiry*).
* Siswa melakukan check-in menggunakan kode presensi serta melihat riwayat kehadiran.
* Halaman: `/attendance/[courseId]`.

#### 📋 6. Tugas / Assignments (P1)
* Guru membuat tugas dengan deadline dan instruksi.
* Siswa mengumpulkan tugas (teks / link berkas) dan memantau status pengumpulan.
* Guru memberikan penilaian (*grading*) dan feedback.

#### 📊 7. Transkrip Nilai / Grades (P0)
* Rekapitulasi nilai terpusat yang menggabungkan hasil kuis dan tugas secara nyata dari database (bukan nilai dummy).
* Halaman: `/grades` dan `/grades/[courseId]`.

---

### 3. Loop Pembelajaran (The Core Loop)

Alur utama sistem sudah terhubung menjadi satu ekosistem utuh:
$$\text{Belajar (LMS)} \longrightarrow \text{Presensi} \longrightarrow \text{Tugas} \longrightarrow \text{Kuis (King of the Hill)} \longrightarrow \text{Nilai} \longrightarrow \text{AI Analisis Topik Lemah} \longrightarrow \text{Latihan AI Adaptif}$$

---

### 4. Langkah yang Siap Dijalankan / Dilanjutkan

1. **Menjalankan & Verifikasi Lingkungan Lokal**:
   * Menjalankan PostgreSQL (`docker-compose up -d`).

<SKILL>The user has explicitly invoked the (ponytail) skill. You must strictly follow the instructions in this skill to process their request. Here are its contents:
# Ponytail

You are a lazy senior developer. Lazy means efficient, not careless. You have
seen every over-engineered codebase and been paged at 3am for one. The best
code is the code never written.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No drift back to over-building. Still active if
unsure. Off only: "stop ponytail" / "normal mode". Default: **full**.
Switch: `/ponytail lite|full|ultra`.

## The ladder

Stop at the first rung that holds:

1. **Does this need to exist at all?** Speculative need = skip it, say so in one line. (YAGNI)
2. **Already in this codebase?** A helper, util, type, or pattern that already lives here → reuse it. Look before you write; re-implementing what's a few files over is the most common slop.
3. **Stdlib does it?** Use it.
4. **Native platform feature covers it?** `<input type="date">` over a picker lib, CSS over JS, DB constraint over app code.
5. **Already-installed dependency solves it?** Use it. Never add a new one for what a few lines can do.
6. **Can it be one line?** One line.
7. **Only then:** the minimum code that works.

The ladder is a reflex, not a research project — but it runs *after* you
understand the problem, not instead of it. Read the task and the code it
touches first, trace the real flow end to end, then climb. Two rungs work →
take the higher one and move on. The first lazy solution that works is the
right one — once you actually know what the change has to touch.

**Bug fix = root cause, not symptom.** A report names a symptom. Before you
edit, grep every caller of the function you're about to touch. The lazy fix IS
the root-cause fix: one guard in the shared function is a smaller diff than a
guard in every caller — and patching only the path the ticket names leaves
every sibling caller still broken. Fix it once, where all callers route through.

## Rules

- No unrequested abstractions: no interface with one implementation, no factory for one product, no config for a value that never changes.
- No boilerplate, no scaffolding "for later", later can scaffold for itself.
- Deletion over addition. Boring over clever, clever is what someone decodes at 3am.
- Fewest files possible. Shortest working diff wins — but only once you understand the problem. The smallest change in the wrong place isn't lazy, it's a second bug.
- Complex request? Ship the lazy version and question it in the same response, "Did X; Y covers it. Need full X? Say so." Never stall on an answer you can default.
- Two stdlib options, same size? Take the one that's correct on edge cases. Lazy means writing less code, not picking the flimsier algorithm.
- Mark deliberate simplifications that cut a real corner with a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic) with a `ponytail:` comment naming the ceiling and upgrade path (`# ponytail: global lock, per-account locks if throughput matters`).

## Output

Code first. Then at most three short lines: what was skipped, when to add it.
No essays, no feature tours, no design notes. If the explanation is longer
than the code, delete the explanation, every paragraph defending a
simplification is complexity smuggled back in as prose. Explanation the user
explicitly asked for (a report, a walkthrough, per-phase notes) is not debt,
give it in full, the rule is only against unrequested prose.

Pattern: `[code] → skipped: [X], add when [Y].`

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **lite** | Build what's asked, but name the lazier alternative in one line. User picks. |
| **full** | The ladder enforced. Stdlib and native first. Shortest diff, shortest explanation. Default. |
| **ultra** | YAGNI extremist. Deletion before addition. Ship the one-liner and challenge the rest of the requirement in the same breath. |

Example: "Add a cache for these API responses."
- lite: "Done, cache added. FYI: `functools.lru_cache` covers this in one line if you'd rather not own a cache class."
- full: "`@lru_cache(maxsize=1000)` on the fetch function. Skipped custom cache class, add when lru_cache measurably falls short."
- ultra: "No cache until a profiler says so. When it does: `@lru_cache`. A hand-rolled TTL cache class is a bug farm with a hit rate."

## When NOT to be lazy

Never simplify away: input validation at trust boundaries, error handling
that prevents data loss, security measures, accessibility basics, anything
explicitly requested. User insists on the full version → build it, no
re-arguing.

Never lazy about understanding the problem. The ladder shortens the
solution, never the reading. Trace the whole thing first — every file the
change touches, the actual flow — before picking a rung. Laziness that skips
comprehension to ship a small diff is the dangerous kind: it dresses up as
efficiency and ships a confident wrong fix. Read fully, then be lazy.

Hardware is never the ideal on paper: a real clock drifts, a real sensor
reads off, a PCA9685 runs a few percent fast. Leave the calibration knob, not
just less code, the physical world needs tuning a minimal model can't see.

Lazy code without its check is unfinished. Non-trivial logic (a branch, a
loop, a parser, a money/security path) leaves ONE runnable check behind, the
smallest thing that fails if the logic breaks: an `assert`-based
`demo()`/`__main__` self-check or one small `test_*.py`. No frameworks, no
fixtures, no per-function suites unless asked. Trivial one-liners need no
test, YAGNI applies to tests too.

## Boundaries

Ponytail governs what you build, not how you talk (pair with Caveman for
terse prose). "stop ponytail" / "normal mode": revert. Level persists until
changed or session end.

The shortest path to done is the right path.</SKILL>
</ADDITIONAL_METADATA>

1: import { Response, NextFunction } from "express"
2: import { AuthRequest } from "../middleware/auth"
3: import { prisma } from "../config/database"
4: import { z } from "zod"

6: // ─── Quiz Session ────────────────────────────────────────
7: 
8: const createQuizSessionSchema = z.object({
9:   title: z.string().min(1),
10:   description: z.string().optional(),
11:   isKingOfTheHill: z.boolean().default(false),
12:   topic: z.string().optional(),
13:   difficulty: z.enum(["easy", "medium", "hard"]).optional(),
14:   questions: z.array(z.object({
15:     question: z.string(),
16:     options: z.array(z.string()),
17:     correctOptionIndex: z.number(),
18:     topic: z.string(),
19:     difficulty: z.string(),
20:     order: z.number(),
21:   })).optional(),
22: })
23: 
24: export async function createQuizSession(req: AuthRequest, res: Response, next: NextFunction) {
25:   try {
26:     const parsed = createQuizSessionSchema.safeParse(req.body)
27:     if (!parsed.success) return res.status(400).json({ error: parsed.error.errors })
28: 
29:     const courseId = parseInt(req.params.courseId)
30:     const course = await prisma.course.findUnique({ where: { id: courseId } })
31:     if (!course) return res.status(404).json({ error: "Course not found" })
32:     if (course.teacherId !== req.user!.id) return res.status(403).json({ error: "Not the teacher" })
33: 
34:     const session = await prisma.quizSession.create({
35:       data: {
36:         title: parsed.data.title,
37:         description: parsed.data.description,
38:         isKingOfTheHill: parsed.data.isKingOfTheHill,
39:         courseId: course.id,
40:         quizQuestions: parsed.data.questions
41:           ? {
42:               create: parsed.data.questions.map((q) => ({
43:                 question: q.question,
44:                 topic: q.topic ?? "General",
45:                 difficulty: (q.difficulty ?? "MEDIUM").toUpperCase() as "EASY" | "MEDIUM" | "HARD",
46:                 order: q.order,
47:                 options: {
48:                   create: q.options.map((opt, idx) => ({
49:                     text: opt,
50:                     isCorrect: idx === q.correctOptionIndex,
51:                     order: idx,
52:                   })),
53:                 },
54:               })),
55:             }
56:           : undefined,
57:       },
58:     })
59: 
60:     res.status(201).json(session)
61:   } catch (err) {
62:     next(err)
63:   }
64: }
65: 
66: export async function getQuizSession(req: AuthRequest, res: Response) {
67:   const session = await prisma.quizSession.findUnique({
68:     where: { id: parseInt(req.params.sessionId) },
69:     include: {
70:       quizQuestions: {
71:         orderBy: { order: "asc" },
72:         include: { options: { orderBy: { order: "asc" } } },
73:       },
74:     },
75:   })
76: 
77:   if (!session) return res.status(404).json({ error: "Quiz session not found" })
78: 
79:   // Verify user is enrolled in the course
80:   const enrolled = await prisma.enrollment.findUnique({
81:     where: {
82:       userId_courseId: { userId: req.user!.id, courseId: session.courseId },
83:     },
84:   })
85:   if (!enrolled && req.user!.role !== "TEACHER") {
86:     return res.status(403).json({ error: "Not enrolled in this course" })
87:   }
88: 
89:   // Strip isCorrect from options — students shouldn't see the answer
90:   const sanitized = {
91:     ...session,
92:     quizQuestions: session.quizQuestions.map((q) => ({
93:       ...q,
94:       options: q.options.map(({ isCorrect, ...rest }) => rest),
95:     })),
96:   }
97: 
98:   res.json(sanitized)
99: }
100: 
101: export async function listQuizSessions(req: AuthRequest, res: Response) {
102:   const courseId = parseInt(req.params.courseId)
103:   const enrolled = await prisma.enrollment.findUnique({
104:     where: { userId_courseId: { userId: req.user!.id, courseId } },
105:   })
106:   if (!enrolled && req.user!.role !== "TEACHER") {
107:     return res.status(403).json({ error: "Not enrolled in this course" })
108:   }
109: 
110:   const sessions = await prisma.quizSession.findMany({
111:     where: { courseId },
112:     include: { _count: { select: { quizQuestions: true } } },
113:     orderBy: { createdAt: "desc" },
114:   })
115: 
116:   res.json(sessions)
117: }

123:   questionId: z.number(),
124:   optionId: z.number(),
125:   responseTimeMs: z.number().int().min(0),

6:   const sessionId = parseInt(req.params.sessionId)
7: 
8:   // Verify session exists
9:   const session = await prisma.quizSession.findUnique({

13: 
14:   // Verify user is enrolled
15:   const enrolled = await prisma.enrollment.findUnique({
16:     where: { userId_courseId: { userId: req.user!.id, courseId: session.courseId } },
17:   })
18:   if (!enrolled && req.user!.role !== "TEACHER") {
19:     return res.status(403).json({ error: "Not enrolled in this course" })
20:   }
21: 
22:   // Build leaderboard from quiz answers (computed server-side, not trusted from client)
23:   const entries = await prisma.$queryRaw<
24:     Array<{
25:       userId: number
26:       score: number
27:       correctCount: number
28:       avgResponseMs: number
29:       rank: number
30:       name: string | null
31:       email: string
32:     }>
33:   >`
34:     SELECT
35:       u.id as "userId",
36:       u."name" as "name",
37:       u."email" as "email",
38:       COALESCE(SUM(qa.points), 0) as "score",
39:       SUM(CASE WHEN qa."isCorrect" THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as "correctCount",
40:       COALESCE(AVG(qa."responseTimeMs"), 0) as "avgResponseMs",
41:       RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(SUM(qa.points), 0) DESC) as "rank"
42:     FROM "User" u
43:     LEFT JOIN "QuizAnswer" qa ON qa."userId" = u.id AND qa."quizSessionId" = ${sessionId}
44:     WHERE qa."userId" IS NOT NULL
45:     GROUP BY u.id, u."name", u."email"
46:     ORDER BY "score" DESC
47:     LIMIT 50
48:   `
49: 
50:   const king = entries[0]
51:   const kingOfTheHill = king
52:     ? {
53:         userId: king.userId,
54:         name: king.name ?? king.email,
55:         score: Number(king.score),
56:         correctCount: Number(king.correctCount),
57:         avgResponseMs: Math.round(Number(king.avgResponseMs)),
58:       }
59:     : null
60:

67:       name: e.name ?? e.email,

Berikut adalah hasil **System & Codebase Audit** menyeluruh untuk platform **Aksara** sesuai instruksi Step 1 sebelum memulai perubahan kode.

---

### A. Current Architecture Assessment

#### Yang Sudah Bagus
1. **Fondasi Data Relasional Lengkap**: Schema Prisma (`schema.prisma`) memiliki relasi yang terstruktur dari User, Course, Module, Progress, Quiz, Assessment, hingga AI Session.
2. **Server-Side Scoring**: Logika kalkulasi poin kuis dan validasi jawaban dilakukan 100% di backend (`quiz.controller.ts`), mencegah manipulasi skor di sisi klien.
3. **AI Provider Abstraction**: Implementasi provider interface (`ai.provider.ts`, `mimo.provider.ts`, `longcat.provider.ts`) sudah rapi dan aman (API key tidak terekspos ke frontend).
4. **Clean Code Structure**: Pola Express modular (Routes, Controllers, Middleware, Services) dan Next.js App Router yang terisolasi dengan baik.

#### Yang Bermasalah / Butuh Perbaikan
1. **Disconnected Mastery Loop**: Hasil latihan AI (`TrainingSession` & `GeneratedQuestion`) belum meng-update status `WeakTopic` atau metrik penguasaan materi (*Mastery Score*), sehingga loop remedial belum tertutup.
2. **Bug pada Query Ranking Individu**: Di [`getUserRank`](file:///home/ridanxd/m-one/api/src/controllers/leaderboard.controller.ts#L91-L110), fungsi `RANK() OVER()` dijalankan setelah klausul `WHERE u.id = ?`, yang menyebabkan rank selalu bernilai `1` karena di-filter sebelum dihitung peringkatnya.
3. **Kalkulasi Max Score Arbitrer**: Di [`getGrades`](file:///home/ridanxd/m-one/api/src/controllers/grade.controller.ts#L38), nilai `maxScore` kuis di-hardcode dengan `totalCount * 100 + 75` alih-alih dihitung dari parameter sesi sebenarnya.
4. **Teacher Intelligence Terbatas**: Endpoint teacher overview baru mengembalikan data mentah tanpa agregasi tingkat kesulitan topik atau deteksi siswa yang tertinggal (*at-risk*).

---

### B. Feature Gap Analysis

| Area | Current State | Problem | Improvement | Priority |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Topic Mastery Engine** | Hanya status biner `WeakTopic` (<70% accuracy) per `quizResultId`. | Tidak ada tracking penguasaan topik jangka panjang; tidak bisa melihat tren perkembangan siswa. | Buat kalkulasi **Topic Mastery** terpadu per siswa (Score 0–100, Tren: Naik/Turun/Stabil, Confidence). | **P0** |
| **Adaptive Feedback Loop** | Training AI menghasilkan soal, disimpan, tetapi selesai tanpa evaluasi dampak. | Tidak bisa membuktikan apakah latihan AI berhasil meningkatkan pemahaman siswa. | Simpan metrik **Pre vs Post-Training Accuracy** dan perbarui status topik lemah setelah sesi latihan selesai. | **P0** |
| **Leaderboard & Ranking** | Query SQL ranking individual `getUserRank` cacat logika (`RANK()` setelah `WHERE`). | Siswa selalu melihat ranking 1 untuk diri sendiri di widget status. | Perbaiki CTE / subquery ranking di SQL agar mengevaluasi seluruh partisipan kuis. | **P0** |
| **Personalized Recommendation** | Dashboard hanya menampilkan daftar kursus dan menu statis. | Siswa tidak tahu langkah terbaik selanjutnya (*next best action*). | Endpoint `/api/student/recommendations` berbasis topik paling lemah + deadline tugas terdekat. | **P1** |
| **Teacher Intelligence** | Endpoint guru hanya memuat daftar nama dan jumlah kuis statis (`quizResults: 0`). | Guru tidak mendapat insight topik apa yang paling sulit bagi sekelas atau siswa mana yang butuh remedial. | Agregasi **Class Mastery**, daftar siswa *At-Risk*, dan rekomendasi intervensi materi untuk guru. | **P1** |
| **AI Question Fallback & Guard** | AI generation langsung di-parse; bila gagal hanya melempar status 502. | Jika provider timeout atau response format cacat, flow belajar terputus. | Parser schema Zod yang lebih toleran + template fallback deterministik terverifikasi. | **P1** |
| **Competitive Analytics** | Leaderboard hanya ranking global dan skor agregat. | Siswa di peringkat bawah kehilangan motivasi kompetisi. | Tambahkan metrik *Personal Best*, *Streak Record*, dan *Speed Percentile*. | **P2** |

---

### C. Competition Differentiation & "Wow Moment"

1. **Diferensiasi Utama dari LMS Konvensional**:
   LMS konvensional berhenti pada evaluasi (memberi nilai kuis/tugas). **Aksara bertindak sebagai loop diagnostik dan kuratif otomatis**: mendeteksi kelemahan spesifik per konsep, membuatkan remedial personal via AI, dan mengukur kenaikan penguasaan (*measurable learning outcome*).
2. **"Wow Moment" saat Live Demo**:
   *Siswa mengerjakan Kuis $\rightarrow$ Kalah skor & gagal di topik tertentu $\rightarrow$ Sistem otomatis menandai topik lemah $\rightarrow$ AI menyusun sesi latihan instan $\rightarrow$ Siswa menyelesaikan latihan $\rightarrow$ Grafik Mastery naik secara real-time $\rightarrow$ Dashboard Guru langsung mencatat penurunan persentase siswa bermasalah di topik tersebut.*
3. **Fitur Terkuat untuk Tema Edukasi**:
   **Continuous Adaptive Remediation Loop** — Pembuktian nyata peningkatan akurasi (*e.g., Topic X: 40% $\rightarrow$ 85%*) berbasis data aktual.

---

### D. Feature Roadmap

#### Phase 1: P0 (Critical Integrity & Closed Loop)
* [ ] **Fix Leaderboard Query**: Perbaiki subquery/window function pada [`getUserRank`](file:///home/ridanxd/m-one/api/src/controllers/leaderboard.controller.ts).
* [ ] **Topic Mastery Engine**: Implementasi kalkulasi skor penguasaan topik kumulatif per siswa.
* [ ] **Closed Remediation Loop**: Update status penguasaan topik dan log perbandingan performa *before-vs-after* pasca latihan AI.
* [ ] **Grade Consistency**: Standardisasi kalkulasi `maxScore` dan pembobotan kuis vs tugas.

#### Phase 2: P1 (High Value Intelligence)
* [ ] **Teacher Actionable Analytics**: Diagnostik kelas (Topik tersulit, rasio kelulusan konsep, daftar siswa *At-Risk*).
* [ ] **Smart Next-Action Engine**: Rekomendasi kontekstual di dashboard siswa (fokus topik terlemah + materi terkait).
* [ ] **AI Fault-Tolerance**: Validasi schema Zod ketat dan fallback gracefully saat model AI lambat/gagal.

#### Phase 3: P2 (Motivation & Polish)
* [ ] **Competitive Badges & Milestones**: Personal best streak, speed percentile, dan comeback metric.

---

### E. Technical Debt yang Harus Dibereskan

1. **SQL Window Function Bug**: File [`api/src/controllers/leaderboard.controller.ts`](file:///home/ridanxd/m-one/api/src/controllers/leaderboard.controller.ts#L91-L124) memerlukan CTE agar ranking dihitung terhadap seluruh kelas sebelum filtering user.
2. **Hardcoded Data di Controller Guru**: File [`api/src/controllers/grade.controller.ts`](file:///home/ridanxd/m-one/api/src/controllers/grade.controller.ts#L112-L113) mengembalikan hardcoded `quizResults: 0, grades: 0`.
3. **Database Indexing**: Kurangnya composite index pada tabel `QuizAnswer(quizSessionId, userId)` dan `WeakTopic(quizResultId, topic)` yang akan memperlambat query analitik seiring bertambahnya data kuis.

---

### Langkah Berikutnya

Jika roadmap di atas sudah sesuai, kita akan mulai mengeksekusi **Phase 1 (P0)**: memperbaiki bug query ranking, mengimplementasikan **Topic Mastery Engine**, dan menutup **Remediation Loop**.

1: #!/usr/bin/env bash
2: # caveman — installer shim.
3: #
4: # Thin wrapper around bin/install.js (the unified Node installer). Every flag
5: # you'd pass to bin/install.js can be passed here; we just forward them.
6: #
7: # One-line install:
8: #   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/v1.10.0/install.sh | bash
9: #   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/v1.10.0/install.sh | bash -s -- --all
10: #
11: # Local clone:
12: #   bash install.sh [flags]
13: #
14: # Why a Node installer? install.sh + install.ps1 used to be parallel sources
15: # of truth and constantly drifted (issue #249, etc.). One Node script works
16: # everywhere without bash/PowerShell quoting bugs.
17: 
18: set -euo pipefail
19: 
20: REPO="JuliusBrussee/caveman"
21: PINNED_REF="${CAVEMAN_REF:-v3.1.0}"
22: 
23: # Require Node ≥18. nvm is a common path; print a hint if missing.
24: if ! command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then
25:   echo "caveman: Node.js (≥18) required. Install:" >&2
26:   echo "  macOS:  brew install node" >&2
27:   echo "  Linux:  see https://nodejs.org or use nvm (https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm)" >&2
28:   exit 1
29: fi
30: 
31: NODE_MAJOR=$(node -p "process.versions.node.split('.')[0]")
32: if [ "$NODE_MAJOR" -lt 18 ]; then
33:   echo "caveman: Node $NODE_MAJOR too old. Need Node ≥18." >&2
34:   echo "  Upgrade: https://nodejs.org" >&2
35:   exit 1
36: fi
37: 
38: # If we're inside the repo clone, run the local installer directly — saves
39: # the npx round-trip and keeps offline installs working. BASH_SOURCE is unset
40: # when bash is invoked from stdin (curl | bash). Do not feed an empty value to
41: # dirname: dirname "" resolves to "." and would execute an unrelated
42: # $PWD/bin/install.js from the caller's checkout.
43: here=""
44: source_path="${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-}"
45: if [ -n "$source_path" ]; then
46:   here="$(cd "$(dirname "$source_path")" 2>/dev/null && pwd)" || here=""
47: fi
48: if [ -n "$here" ] && [ -f "$here/bin/install.js" ]; then
49:   exec node "$here/bin/install.js" "$@"
50: fi
51: 
52: # Curl-pipe path: delegate to npx. We do NOT pass `--` here — npm 7+ npx
53: # already forwards trailing args to the package, and a literal `--` tripped
54: # bin/install.js's parseArgs as an unknown flag.
55: if ! command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
56:   echo "caveman: npx required (ships with Node ≥18). Reinstall Node.js." >&2
57:   exit 1
58: fi
59: 
60: exec npx -y "github:$REPO#$PINNED_REF" "$@"
61:

The current local time is: 2026-10-06T09:32:55+07:00.

The user has mentioned some items in the form @[ITEM]. Here is extra information about the items that were mentioned by the user, in the order that they appear:

/caveman is a [Slash Command]:
<SKILL>The user has explicitly invoked the (caveman) skill. You must strictly follow the instructions in this skill to process their request. Here are its contents:
# caveman

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

Caveman is a voice, not broken grammar. Reader pays per token and reads in a terminal. Every word earns its place. Every fact survives.

## Persistence

Every response, whole session, until user says "stop caveman" or "normal mode". Unsure if still on? It is. Confirm the switch-off in one line.

`/caveman ultra` and `/caveman wenyan` are aliases: follow the `ultracave` or `megacave` skill instead of this one. `/caveman status` reports the mode and changes nothing. Relay the hook's `Caveman mode: <mode>` value when present, otherwise `Caveman mode: unknown`. Never infer a mode from the configured default.

## Why

1. Every output token is billed and read. Filler costs twice.
2. Code, commands, paths, numbers, errors are the payload. One changed character breaks them.
3. Ceremony is expensive, grammar is cheap. "Sure, I'd be happy to help" is ten tokens. "the" is one.
4. A dropped negation costs more than every token saved. Clarity beats compression.

## Rules

### 1. Answer first

Answer, then reason, then next step. Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Bad: "Sure! I'd be happy to help. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Good: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

### 2. Kill ceremony

No greeting, hedging, pleasantries, recap, or closer. No "Sure!", "Let me", "I'll now", "Hope this helps". No just/really/basically/actually/simply.

### 3. Short word

"fix" not "implement a solution for". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.

### 4. Articles optional, meaning never

Drop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. Numbers and units exact.

Bad: "Migration drop column backup first."
Good: "Back up first. Then run migration: it drops the column."

### 5. One idea per sentence

ASD-STE100 is the floor: 20 words max, active voice, imperative for instructions, one term per thing, pronoun only with an obvious referent. Compression and clarity conflict? Clarity wins.

### 6. Payload verbatim

Code blocks unchanged. Commands, paths, API names exact. Errors quoted exact, shortest decisive line only.

### 7. Tool runs: bounded status

No text between routine calls. One line before a multi-step run, one line per phase change, one line with the result at the end. Otherwise text before a call only to clarify, warn, or disambiguate.

### 8. User's language

Compress the style, not the language. An explicit reply-language instruction wins. Never switch because of quoted text. Technical terms and errors stay verbatim. Particles and case markers are grammar, not filler.

### 9. Never perform caveman

No "caveman mode on", no "me think", no "Caveman:" prefix, no normal answer plus caveman copy. No decorative tables or emoji. Never add a word to sound caveman. Caveman phrasing not shorter than plain? Use plain.

## When to break the rules

Plain prose, then resume:

1. Security warning.
2. Irreversible action. Confirm in full sentences first.
3. Step order a fragment could scramble.
4. User confused or repeats the question.
5. Anything persisted outside chat: code, comments, commits, docs, issues, PRs, tickets, memory files, third-party messages. `/caveman-compress` exempt.
6. Harness asks for a status line or confirmation. Give it. Harness decides *when* you speak, caveman decides *how*.

## Pre-send check

1. First sentence announces what you will do? Delete.
2. Last sentence recaps or offers help? Delete.
3. Every not/never/no/only present? Every code span, path, number, error verbatim?
4. Any sentence with two readings? Make it a full sentence.</SKILL>
</ADDITIONAL_METADATA>

294: # 5. PRE-TRAINING VS POST-TRAINING
295: 
296: Buat pengukuran yang jelas.
297: 
298: Minimal:
299: 
300: ```text
301: preTrainingAccuracy
302: postTrainingAccuracy
303: improvement
304: ```
305: 
306: Jika memungkinkan:
307: 
308: ```text
309: preMastery
310: postMastery
311: masteryDelta
312: ```
313: 
314: Sistem harus dapat menjawab:
315: 
316: > "Apakah intervensi AI berhasil?"
317: 
318: Jika tidak berhasil:
319: 
320: ```text
321: Mastery tidak naik
322: ```
323: 
324: maka sistem harus dapat mengidentifikasi bahwa student masih membutuhkan remedial.
325: 
326: ---
327: 
328: # 6. ADAPTIVE QUESTION ENGINE
329: 
330: AI tidak boleh menghasilkan soal secara random.
331: 
332: Gunakan context:
333: 
334: ```text
335: student
336: course
337: topic
338: mastery
339: weakness
340: previous mistakes
341: difficulty
342: previous questions
343: training history
344: ```
345: 
346: Contoh:
347: 
348: Student:
349: 
350: ```text
351: SQL JOIN
352: Mastery: 35
353: Repeated error:
354: confuses LEFT JOIN and INNER JOIN
355: ```
356: 
357: Maka AI harus diarahkan untuk memberikan latihan yang relevan dengan kesalahan tersebut.
358: 
359: Training dapat bergerak:
360: 
361: ```text
362: concept
363: ↓
364: easy application
365: ↓
366: normal problem
367: ↓
368: scenario
369: ↓
370: harder application
371: ↓
372: assessment
373: ```
374: 
375: Jika mastery sudah tinggi, tingkatkan difficulty.
376: 
377: Jika rendah, berikan remedial yang lebih fundamental.
378: 
379: ---
380: 
381: # 7. PREVENT QUESTION REPETITION
382: 
383: AI jangan terus menghasilkan soal yang sama.
384: 
385: Simpan atau gunakan history untuk mencegah:
386: 
387: * duplicate questions
388: * duplicate answer pattern
389: * repeated scenario
390: * repeated wording
391: 
392: Jika database sudah menyimpan generated questions, manfaatkan data tersebut.
393: 
394: ---
395: 
396: # 8. AI OUTPUT VALIDATION
397: 
398: Jangan percaya raw AI response.
399: 
400: Implementasikan structured validation.
401: 
402: Gunakan schema validation yang sesuai dengan architecture existing, misalnya Zod jika cocok dengan codebase.
403: 
404: Validasi:
405: 
406: * question
407: * options
408: * correct answer
409: * explanation
410: * topic
411: * difficulty
412: * metadata yang diperlukan
413: 
414: Jika AI:
415: 
416: ```text
417: timeout
418: invalid JSON
419: missing field
420: wrong schema
421: empty response
422: ```
423: 
424: jangan membuat aplikasi crash.
425: 
426: Buat fallback yang aman.
427: 
428: Fallback boleh deterministic/template-based selama tetap valid secara pedagogis.
429: 
430: ---
431: 
432: # 9. AI PROVIDER RESILIENCE
433: 
434: Provider abstraction yang sudah ada harus benar-benar berguna.
435: 
436: Jika provider utama gagal:
437: 
438: ```text
439: Provider A
440: ↓
441: failure
442: ↓
443: Provider B
444: ```
445: 
446: jika architecture memungkinkan.
447: 
448: Pastikan:
449: 
450: * timeout
451: * retry terbatas
452: * error handling
453: * provider fallback
454: * logging
455: * API key tetap server-side
456: 
457: Jangan menyebabkan request menggantung tanpa batas.
458: 
459: ---
460: 
461: # 10. STUDENT LEARNING PROFILE
462: 
463: Bangun learning profile berdasarkan data nyata.
464: 
465: Profile harus dapat mencerminkan:
466: 
467: ```text
468: overall mastery
469: strong topics
470: weak topics
471: improving topics
472: declining topics
473: quiz performance
474: training performance
475: assignment performance
476: attendance
477: learning consistency
478: ```
479: 
480: Jangan membuat personality profiling yang tidak memiliki dasar data.
481: 
482: Fokus pada learning performance.
483: 
484: ---
485: 
486: # 11. NEXT BEST ACTION ENGINE
487: 
488: Ini salah satu fitur yang akan membuat Aksara terasa intelligent.
489: 
490: Sistem harus dapat menentukan:
491: 
492: > "Apa tindakan paling berguna yang harus dilakukan student sekarang?"
493: 
494: Contoh:
495: 
496: ```text
497: Priority:
498: Practice SQL JOIN
499: 
500: Reason:
501: Mastery 42%
502: 
503: Recommended:
504: 5 adaptive questions
505: 
506: Related material:
507: SQL JOIN Fundamentals
508: 
509: Deadline:
510: Assignment due tomorrow
511: ```
512: 
513: Prioritas dapat mempertimbangkan:
514: 
515: ```text
516: weakness
517: mastery
518: deadline
519: recent decline
520: unfinished material
521: training history
522: ```
523: 
524: Jangan hanya menampilkan daftar menu.
525: 
526: Berikan rekomendasi yang benar-benar kontekstual.
527: 
528: ---
529: 
530: # 12. STUDENT DASHBOARD DATA
531: 
532: Pastikan dashboard siswa dapat mengambil insight dari engine tadi.

541: Recent Performance

548: 
549: Yang penting data benar-benar berasal dari backend.

552: 
553: # 13. TEACHER INTELLIGENCE
554: 
555: Guru harus mendapatkan manfaat dari seluruh data yang dikumpulkan Aksara.
556:

558:

566: Declining Students

572: Guru harus bisa mengetahui:

575: 
576: dan:
577: 
578: > "Siswa mana yang membutuhkan intervensi?"
579: 
580: ---
581: 
582: # 14. AT-RISK DETECTION
583: 
584: Buat detection yang explainable.
585: 
586: Jangan hanya:
587: 
588: ```text
589: atRisk = true
590: ```
591: 
592: Simpan alasan.
593: 
594: Contoh:
595: 
596: ```text
597: AT RISK
598: 
599: Reasons:
600: - mastery declining
601: - quiz accuracy < threshold
602: - assignment completion low
603: - attendance declining
604: ```
605: 
606: Gunakan beberapa sinyal, bukan satu angka saja.
607: 
608: ---
609:

631: + 5 adaptive practice questions
632: ```
633: 
634: Dengan begitu Aksara membantu guru mengambil keputusan.

/caveman is a [Slash Command]:
<SKILL>The user has explicitly invoked the (caveman) skill. You must strictly follow the instructions in this skill to process their request. Here are its contents:
# caveman

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

Caveman is a voice, not broken grammar. Reader pays per token and reads in a terminal. Every word earns its place. Every fact survives.

## Persistence

Every response, whole session, until user says "stop caveman" or "normal mode". Unsure if still on? It is. Confirm the switch-off in one line.

`/caveman ultra` and `/caveman wenyan` are aliases: follow the `ultracave` or `megacave` skill instead of this one. `/caveman status` reports the mode and changes nothing. Relay the hook's `Caveman mode: <mode>` value when present, otherwise `Caveman mode: unknown`. Never infer a mode from the configured default.

## Why

1. Every output token is billed and read. Filler costs twice.
2. Code, commands, paths, numbers, errors are the payload. One changed character breaks them.
3. Ceremony is expensive, grammar is cheap. "Sure, I'd be happy to help" is ten tokens. "the" is one.
4. A dropped negation costs more than every token saved. Clarity beats compression.

## Rules

### 1. Answer first

Answer, then reason, then next step. Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Bad: "Sure! I'd be happy to help. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Good: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

### 2. Kill ceremony

No greeting, hedging, pleasantries, recap, or closer. No "Sure!", "Let me", "I'll now", "Hope this helps". No just/really/basically/actually/simply.

### 3. Short word

"fix" not "implement a solution for". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.

### 4. Articles optional, meaning never

Drop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. Numbers and units exact.

Bad: "Migration drop column backup first."
Good: "Back up first. Then run migration: it drops the column."

### 5. One idea per sentence

ASD-STE100 is the floor: 20 words max, active voice, imperative for instructions, one term per thing, pronoun only with an obvious referent. Compression and clarity conflict? Clarity wins.

### 6. Payload verbatim

Code blocks unchanged. Commands, paths, API names exact. Errors quoted exact, shortest decisive line only.

### 7. Tool runs: bounded status

No text between routine calls. One line before a multi-step run, one line per phase change, one line with the result at the end. Otherwise text before a call only to clarify, warn, or disambiguate.

### 8. User's language

Compress the style, not the language. An explicit reply-language instruction wins. Never switch because of quoted text. Technical terms and errors stay verbatim. Particles and case markers are grammar, not filler.

### 9. Never perform caveman

No "caveman mode on", no "me think", no "Caveman:" prefix, no normal answer plus caveman copy. No decorative tables or emoji. Never add a word to sound caveman. Caveman phrasing not shorter than plain? Use plain.

## When to break the rules

Plain prose, then resume:

1. Security warning.
2. Irreversible action. Confirm in full sentences first.
3. Step order a fragment could scramble.
4. User confused or repeats the question.
5. Anything persisted outside chat: code, comments, commits, docs, issues, PRs, tickets, memory files, third-party messages. `/caveman-compress` exempt.
6. Harness asks for a status line or confirmation. Give it. Harness decides *when* you speak, caveman decides *how*.

## Pre-send check

1. First sentence announces what you will do? Delete.
2. Last sentence recaps or offers help? Delete.
3. Every not/never/no/only present? Every code span, path, number, error verbatim?
4. Any sentence with two readings? Make it a full sentence.</SKILL>

11: /**
12:  * Deterministic, explainable Topic Mastery Engine.
13:  * Calculates rolling mastery score (0-100), confidence, and trend.
14:  */
15: export async function updateMasteryFromQuiz(
16:   userId: number,
17:   courseId: number,
18:   topicPerformances: TopicPerformanceInput[]
19: ) {
20:   for (const perf of topicPerformances) {
21:     if (perf.total === 0) continue
22: 
23:     const sessionAccuracy = (perf.correct / perf.total) * 100
24:     const timeSpeedBonus = perf.avgTimeMs
25:       ? perf.avgTimeMs < 3000
26:         ? 5
27:         : perf.avgTimeMs > 10000
28:         ? -5
29:         : 0
30:       : 0
31:     const sessionScore = Math.max(0, Math.min(100, sessionAccuracy + timeSpeedBonus))
32: 
33:     const existing = await prisma.topicMastery.findUnique({
34:       where: {
35:         userId_topic: { userId, topic: perf.topic },
36:       },
37:     })
38: 
39:     if (!existing) {
40:       const initialMastery = Math.round(sessionScore)
41:       const confidence = Math.min(1.0, 0.3 + perf.total * 0.05)
42: 
43:       await prisma.topicMastery.create({
44:         data: {
45:           userId,
46:           courseId,
47:           topic: perf.topic,
48:           masteryScore: initialMastery,
49:           confidence,
50:           attemptCount: perf.total,
51:           correctCount: perf.correct,
52:           accuracy: perf.correct / perf.total,
53:           recentAccuracy: perf.correct / perf.total,
54:           avgResponseMs: perf.avgTimeMs ?? 0,
55:           trend: MasteryTrend.STABLE,
56:           lastPracticedAt: new Date(),
57:         },
58:       })
59:     } else {
60:       const totalAttempts = existing.attemptCount + perf.total
61:       const totalCorrect = existing.correctCount + perf.correct
62:       const overallAccuracy = totalCorrect / totalAttempts
63:       const recentAccuracy = perf.correct / perf.total
64: 
65:       // Rolling alpha: newer attempts have 40% weight, history 60%
66:       const alpha = 0.4
67:       const newMasteryScore = Math.round(alpha * sessionScore + (1 - alpha) * existing.masteryScore)
68: 
69:       // Trend analysis
70:       const delta = newMasteryScore - existing.masteryScore
71:       let trend: MasteryTrend = MasteryTrend.STABLE
72:       if (delta >= 3) trend = MasteryTrend.IMPROVING
73:       else if (delta <= -3) trend = MasteryTrend.DECLINING
74: 
75:       const newAvgTime =
76:         perf.avgTimeMs && existing.avgResponseMs > 0
77:           ? Math.round((existing.avgResponseMs + perf.avgTimeMs) / 2)
78:           : perf.avgTimeMs || existing.avgResponseMs
79: 
80:       const confidence = Math.min(1.0, existing.confidence + 0.1)
81: 
82:       await prisma.topicMastery.update({
83:         where: { id: existing.id },
84:         data: {
85:           courseId: courseId || existing.courseId,
86:           masteryScore: newMasteryScore,
87:           confidence,
88:           attemptCount: totalAttempts,
89:           correctCount: totalCorrect,
90:           accuracy: overallAccuracy,
91:           recentAccuracy,
92:           avgResponseMs: newAvgTime,
93:           trend,
94:           lastPracticedAt: new Date(),
95:         },
96:       })
97:     }
98:   }
99: }

101: /**
102:  * Updates mastery after a student completes an AI training session.
103:  * Closes the AI remediation loop with pre/post evaluation.
104:  */
105: export async function updateMasteryFromTraining(
106:   userId: number,
107:   topic: string,
108:   totalCount: number,
109:   correctCount: number,
110:   courseId?: number
111: ) {
112:   if (totalCount === 0) return null
113: 
114:   const trainingAccuracy = (correctCount / totalCount) * 100
115:   const existing = await prisma.topicMastery.findUnique({
116:     where: {
117:       userId_topic: { userId, topic },
118:     },
119:   })
120: 
121:   const preMastery = existing ? existing.masteryScore : 50.0
122: 
123:   if (!existing) {
124:     const initialMastery = Math.round(trainingAccuracy)
125:     const newRecord = await prisma.topicMastery.create({
126:       data: {
127:         userId,
128:         courseId,
129:         topic,
130:         masteryScore: initialMastery,
131:         confidence: 0.5,
132:         attemptCount: totalCount,
133:         correctCount,
134:         accuracy: correctCount / totalCount,
135:         recentAccuracy: correctCount / totalCount,
136:         avgResponseMs: 0,
137:         trend: initialMastery >= 60 ? MasteryTrend.IMPROVING : MasteryTrend.STABLE,
138:         lastPracticedAt: new Date(),
139:       },
140:     })
141:     return {
142:       preMastery: 50.0,
143:       postMastery: initialMastery,
144:       delta: initialMastery - 50.0,
145:       trend: newRecord.trend,
146:     }
147:   }
148: 
149:   // Weight training heavily (50%) for remedial impact
150:   const alpha = 0.5
151:   const postMastery = Math.round(alpha * trainingAccuracy + (1 - alpha) * existing.masteryScore)
152:   const delta = postMastery - existing.masteryScore
153: 
154:   let trend: MasteryTrend = existing.trend
155:   if (delta >= 2) trend = MasteryTrend.IMPROVING
156:   else if (delta <= -2) trend = MasteryTrend.DECLINING
157: 
158:   const totalAttempts = existing.attemptCount + totalCount
159:   const totalCorrect = existing.correctCount + correctCount
160: 
161:   await prisma.topicMastery.update({
162:     where: { id: existing.id },
163:     data: {
164:       masteryScore: postMastery,
165:       confidence: Math.min(1.0, existing.confidence + 0.15),
166:       attemptCount: totalAttempts,
167:       correctCount: totalCorrect,
168:       accuracy: totalCorrect / totalAttempts,
169:       recentAccuracy: correctCount / totalCount,
170:       trend,
171:       lastPracticedAt: new Date(),
172:     },
173:   })
174: 
175:   return {
176:     preMastery,
177:     postMastery,
178:     delta,
179:     trend,
180:   }
181: }

183: /**
184:  * Aggregates class-level mastery and identifies struggling topics for teachers.
185:  */
186: export async function getClassMasteryAnalytics(courseId: number) {
187:   const masteries = await prisma.topicMastery.findMany({
188:     where: { courseId },
189:     include: { user: { select: { id: true, name: true, email: true } } },
190:   })
191: 
192:   const topicMap: Record<
193:     string,
194:     { totalScore: number; count: number; studentScores: number[]; strugglingCount: number }
195:   > = {}
196: 
197:   for (const m of masteries) {
198:     if (!topicMap[m.topic]) {
199:       topicMap[m.topic] = { totalScore: 0, count: 0, studentScores: [], strugglingCount: 0 }
200:     }
201:     topicMap[m.topic].totalScore += m.masteryScore
202:     topicMap[m.topic].count += 1
203:     topicMap[m.topic].studentScores.push(m.masteryScore)
204:     if (m.masteryScore < 60) {
205:       topicMap[m.topic].strugglingCount += 1
206:     }
207:   }
208: 
209:   const topicSummary = Object.entries(topicMap).map(([topic, data]) => {
210:     const avgMastery = Math.round(data.totalScore / data.count)
211:     const strugglingPct = Math.round((data.strugglingCount / data.count) * 100)
212:     let difficulty: "EASY" | "MEDIUM" | "HARD" = "MEDIUM"
213:     if (avgMastery >= 75) difficulty = "EASY"
214:     else if (avgMastery < 55) difficulty = "HARD"
215: 
216:     return {
217:       topic,
218:       avgMastery,
219:       studentCount: data.count,
220:       strugglingPercentage: strugglingPct,
221:       difficulty,
222:       needsClassIntervention: strugglingPct >= 40,
223:     }
224:   })
225: 
226:   topicSummary.sort((a, b) => a.avgMastery - b.avgMastery)
227:   return topicSummary
228: }

230: /**
231:  * Detects at-risk students with transparent and explainable risk factors.
232:  */
233: export async function getAtRiskStudents(courseId: number) {
234:   const enrollments = await prisma.enrollment.findMany({
235:     where: { courseId },
236:     include: {
237:       user: {
238:         select: {
239:           id: true,
240:           name: true,
241:           email: true,
242:           topicMasteries: { where: { courseId } },
243:           attendanceCheckins: { where: { attendanceSession: { courseId } } },
244:           submissions: { where: { assignment: { courseId } } },
245:           quizResults: { where: { quizSession: { courseId } } },
246:         },
247:       },
248:     },
249:   })
250: 
251:   const totalSessions = await prisma.attendanceSession.count({ where: { courseId } })
252:   const totalAssignments = await prisma.assignment.count({ where: { courseId } })
253: 
254:   const atRiskStudents = []
255: 
256:   for (const enrollment of enrollments) {
257:     const student = enrollment.user
258:     const riskFactors: string[] = []
259: 
260:     // 1. Attendance rate
261:     const checkinCount = student.attendanceCheckins.length
262:     const attendancePct = totalSessions > 0 ? (checkinCount / totalSessions) * 100 : 100
263:     if (totalSessions > 0 && attendancePct < 70) {
264:       riskFactors.push(`Kehadiran rendah (${Math.round(attendancePct)}%)`)
265:     }
266: 
267:     // 2. Assignment completion
268:     const submissionCount = student.submissions.length
269:     const assignmentPct = totalAssignments > 0 ? (submissionCount / totalAssignments) * 100 : 100
270:     if (totalAssignments > 0 && assignmentPct < 60) {
271:       riskFactors.push(`Pengumpulan tugas belum lengkap (${submissionCount}/${totalAssignments})`)
272:     }
273: 
274:     // 3. Quiz & Topic Mastery
275:     const masteries = student.topicMasteries
276:     const lowMasteries = masteries.filter((m) => m.masteryScore < 60)
277:     const decliningMasteries = masteries.filter((m) => m.trend === MasteryTrend.DECLINING)
278: 
279:     if (lowMasteries.length > 0) {
280:       riskFactors.push(
281:         `Topik kritis butuh remedial: ${lowMasteries.map((m) => m.topic).join(", ")}`
282:       )
283:     }
284:     if (decliningMasteries.length > 0) {
285:       riskFactors.push(
286:         `Tren penurunan performa pada: ${decliningMasteries.map((m) => m.topic).join(", ")}`
287:       )
288:     }
289: 
290:     const avgMastery =
291:       masteries.length > 0
292:         ? Math.round(masteries.reduce((acc, m) => acc + m.masteryScore, 0) / masteries.length)
293:         : 50
294: 
295:     if (riskFactors.length > 0) {
296:       atRiskStudents.push({
297:         id: student.id,
298:         name: student.name || student.email,
299:         email: student.email,
300:         avgMastery,
301:         attendancePercentage: Math.round(attendancePct),
302:         assignmentCompletion: `${submissionCount}/${totalAssignments}`,
303:         riskFactors,
304:         recommendedIntervention:
305:           lowMasteries.length > 0
306:             ? `Berikan tugas remedial atau AI adaptive practice pada topik ${lowMasteries[0].topic}`
307:             : "Review kehadiran dan dorong pengerjaan materi LMS yang tertunda",
308:       })
309:     }
310:   }
311: 
312:   return atRiskStudents
313: }
